why_angle: The cited results only give rated capacity and AC outlet specs (RIVER 3 Plus manual copies, EcoFlow and BLUETTI store pages, and a sizing rule in Wh). None says that power stations ship with a low-load auto-off that turns the AC off under the 10–30 W a string of LED lights draws, and none says how to switch it off. This page adds the BLUETTI AC180's ECO rule (on as shipped, 10–30 W, 1–4 h, switchable) and the Jackery 600 Plus rule (on by default, 25 W or less, 12 h). It also adds measured idle draw and runtime arithmetic.

page.title: Power Station for Outdoor Lights: Keep the AC Outlets On All Night
page.h1: Best power station for outdoor lights
page.desc: Many power stations turn their AC outlets off under a small LED-light load. Here is how to stop it, plus capacity, idle draw and nights per charge for 4 units.
page.answer: Short answer. A power station for outdoor lights has to keep its AC outlets on under a small load. Our pick, the BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh capacity, 4 AC outlets), ships with ECO mode on, which turns AC off below 10–30 W after 1–4 hours: switch ECO off before running LED lights overnight.

cells.catch: ECO mode on as shipped: AC turns off under a 10–30 W threshold after 1–4 h. Turn ECO off on the screen or in the app
cells.nights: ≈3.3 (1,005 Wh delivered in smartzone.de's 250 W test ÷ 300 Wh)

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Cost per rated Wh: AC180 $499 ÷ 1,152 Wh = $0.43; DELTA 3 Classic $459 ÷ 1,024 Wh = $0.45; Elite 30 V2 $289.99 ÷ 288 Wh = $1.01; Explorer 1500 Ultra $1,079 ÷ 1,536 Wh = $0.70.
  • Idle draw costs the most when the load is small: The Solar Lab measured 17 W of idle draw on the DELTA 3 Classic. A 20 W LED string on it runs 1,024 ÷ (20 + 17) = 27.7 h, not the 1,024 × 0.83 ÷ 20 = 42.5 h that capacity times efficiency suggests.
  • Small units: the Elite 30 V2 runs a 20 W string for 288 ÷ (20 + 4.5) = 11.8 h before inverter losses, which covers one long evening.
  • AC180 measured: smartzone.de (Michael, October 2024) got 1,005 Wh from AC at 250 W and 1,080 Wh at 1,800 W. At 50 W that is 1,005 ÷ 50 = 20 h, about 3.3 six-hour nights. smartzone.de did not report idle draw, so treat 3.3 as a ceiling.
Your lightsFits
One 10–30 W LED string, one evening, unit under coverElite 30 V2 (11.8 h at 20 W before inverter losses)
30–60 W of patio lights for several nights, unit under coverAC180 with ECO off (≈3.3 nights at 50 W × 6 h)
Lowest price for about 1 kWhDELTA 3 Classic at $459; count 17 W of idle draw on top of your lights
The station has to sit out in the rainExplorer 1500 Ultra (IP65), at $0.70 per Wh

Why string lights go dark halfway through the night

Power stations save battery by turning off outlets that carry little or no load, and LED lights draw very little.

  • BLUETTI AC180: the manual says that in ECO mode “the AC/DC output will automatically turn off if the AC180 is bearing low or no load for a while.” You set the AC threshold to 10–30 W (DC: 5–10 W) and the timer to 1, 2, 3 or 4 hours. smartzone.de reports that ECO is on by default. To switch it off, hold the AC and DC buttons together for 2 seconds while the screen is on and turn ECO off in the menu that opens, or turn it off in the BLUETTI app. With ECO off the outlets stay on until you switch them off. {buy:bluetti-ac180}
  • Jackery Explorer 600 Plus: the manual says Energy Saving Mode is on by default. An AC load of 25 W or less counts as low power, and the outputs turn off after 12 hours. Separately, the whole unit shuts down after 2 hours with no charging or discharging; you can change that time in the Jackery app. To turn Energy Saving Mode off, hold the AC and Main Power buttons until its icon disappears.
  • Plug-in timers and photocells: a timer that cuts the lights during the day leaves the outlet with no load for hours. On the manuals' wording, that zero load can run out the auto-off countdown before dusk. Turn auto-off off before relying on a timer.
  • Cold nights: the AC180 is rated to discharge from -4°F to 104°F, and the Explorer 600 Plus from 14°F to 113°F.
  • Rain: Jackery's 600 Plus manual says not to keep the unit where rain or moisture can reach it. The Explorer 1500 Ultra is the IP65-rated exception.

For a single small string, the Elite 30 V2's 4.5 W standby wastes less than a large unit's inverter. {buy:bluetti-elite-30-v2}

Not recommended

A 286 Wh station such as the EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus is too small for 50 W of lights over a 6-hour night. The Solar Lab measured its inverter at 87% efficiency, so 286 × 0.87 = 249 Wh, and 249 ÷ 50 = 5.0 h: the lights go out an hour before the night is over.
